> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `36680df96b5d376c23047ab4ac3cf83e58e2687d` — the merge of head `3d826adf2685d9c2c878a4618d4eaa6ec5c43ae6` into base `584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 36680df96b5d376c23047ab4ac3cf83e58e2687d && git checkout 36680df96b5d376c23047ab4ac3cf83e58e2687d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff 3d826adf2685d9c2c878a4618d4eaa6ec5c43ae6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff && git merge --no-ff 3d826adf2685d9c2c878a4618d4eaa6ec5c43ae6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 584b4225e1fcbaf5e8bed14d9c280d6347a897ff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key-read-outage.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-key-read-outage.pin.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.tenancy-posture-outage.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.api-key-read-outage.pin.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (fenced; read, unchanged), packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts, packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.test.ts (`TRANSPORT_LEDGER`), packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts (`isMissingTableError`, `MISSING_TABLE`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`computeExecCtx`, `resolveExecCtx`), packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`resolveRequestScope`), packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts (`errorResponseBase`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts (`buildAuthGateSessionReader`, `buildFileReadAuthorizer`, `buildAuthSessionResolver`), packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts; the prose face `.changeset/24299-api-key-read-outage.md` is judged under ②. Base read: merge base `c76e849220cc58d3b22190f0612b805728191bcf`, diff +517/-9 over 6 files, production change in `api-key.ts` alone.

### ① Derived judgments

Every served-set and accept-set change, named:

1. **The seam** (`resolveApiKeyAdmission`, `api-key.ts` 702–718). A `sys_api_key` read that was issued and threw now raises `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('sys_api_key', err)`; the one carve-out is `isMissingTableError(err, 'sys_api_key')`, which still answers `none`. RIGHT. The throw leaves the function before any `none` return, so `resolveAuthzContext` step 1 (`resolve-authz-context.ts` 489) rejects before step 2, the session arm (544), can run; neither `withRequestGrantsMemo` nor the resolver catches it. The same function already gave this answer for its lifecycle-policy source (745, `'api_key_policy'`) and its owner-posture source (860, `'auth_gate'`), so the bare `catch` was the one seam in the function that did not.

2. **Every door that admits keys now answers the outage as `503`, key-only and key-plus-cookie alike.** Production code reaches the seam two ways: through `resolveAuthzContext` (the eight transports `TRANSPORT_LEDGER` pins by set equality, four of them through `resolveRequestExecutionContext`: REST `computeExecCtx` 3244, runtime `resolveExecutionContext` 157, settings `verifiedContextFromRequest` 341, the storage download authorizer 1498) and through the one direct call in the storage gate reader (`storage-service-plugin.ts` 1280). Each relays the brand, read in the cited code:
   - REST: `computeExecCtx`'s outer catch returns `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable(err)` (3354); the `GET /data/:object` handler's catch maps the thrown declared envelope through `mapDataError` to its own status (`crud-routes.ts` 166–170). Pinned on the real route: key-only `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, key-plus-cookie `503` with `findData` never called.
   - runtime dispatcher: `resolveRequestScope`'s net re-raises by brand (`http-dispatcher.ts` 762); `errorResponseBase` reads `err.status` (`dispatcher-plugin.ts` 699). The flipped pin asserts brand, `503` and `object === 'sys_api_key'` at the identity step and `executionContext` left undefined; the wire render of this class is the file's existing §2 pin.
   - settings: the resolver re-raises by brand (`settings-service-plugin.ts` 373) and the family door relays (`relayAuthzStoreOutage`, `settings-routes.ts` 151). Pinned on the booted `GET /api/settings`, session read count 0 for key-plus-cookie.
   - storage: the gate reader calls the seam BEFORE its session read (1280 before 1293), and `admission.outcome !== 'none'` returned `undefined` only for a verdict, so the old `none` fell on to the session's posture; the throw now leaves the reader and `refuseHeldSession` relays it with `sendError(res, err.status, err.code, err.message)` (`storage-routes.ts` 660–665). The download authorizer re-raises by brand (1567) and `authorizeDownload` relays (563). The upload door's `buildAuthSessionResolver` (1187) reads the session only and never calls the seam: unchanged.
   - datasource (`admin-routes.ts` 527), sharing (`sharing-plugin.ts` 995), marketplace install-local (3594) and print (151, a relay) re-raise by brand; cloud-connection's three connection-changing doors re-raise (481) while `status` withholds details and logs (517), by its own design; MCP stdio: the `.catch` at `plugin.ts` 526 rewraps only the lifecycle brand, so the outage escapes and the boot refuses, loud; hono current-user passes `headers: undefined` (session-only, the key arm never runs): unchanged.

3. **No remaining path where a key-led request whose read failed falls on to another credential.** `extractApiKey` (`api-key.ts` 90) is the only header reader in the repo: `x-api-key`, then `Authorization: ApiKey`, then `Bearer osk_…`; an unprefixed bearer or a JWT-shaped bearer is never a key, so those are session-only callers. The MCP face passes `session: 'none'` for an unverified JWT but still runs the key arm first. The only caller outside `resolveAuthzContext` (the storage gate reader) throws before its own `getSession`. The runtime pin's old "plain engine fault under a key degrades to a guest" assertion was the single pin of the old answer; it is flipped with the superseded assertion quoted, and its degrade-to-anonymous intent is kept on a throwing session read, which the composition's `readSession` (`request-execution-context.ts` 263) and the resolver's session arm (`catch {}` at 567) still swallow. `resolve-authz-context.ts` needs no change: its blob on this head equals the merge base's, and the fence for PR #24373 holds.

4. **The missing-table carve-out.** RIGHT, and precise enough. `isMissingTableError` keys on SQLSTATE `42P01`, `ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE`, errno 1146 and three dialect phrases, excludes column and sub-object codes and phrases up front, and with `readObject` given refuses a phrase naming another relation (`excludedByReadObject`); anything unrecognised is `false`, so an outage stays loud by default. A connection reset, timeout or permission denial carries none of these. The false-positive direction (a driver composing a missing-table phrase over an outage) is the risk the 2026-08-30 ruling signed off for this predicate on security paths, verbatim beside `tryFind` (`resolve-authz-context.ts` 396–433), and the two-direction pins it requires are present: both dialect spellings answer `none`, a plain fault is loud, a phrase naming `main.some_other_base` is loud. The other direction (a real missing table on a dialect the predicate does not know) answers `503`, which is exactly what `tryFind` already answers that deployment's session callers, so the two arms stay consistent. Option A (throw on every failure) would answer `503` to every key-bearing request on the supported `ABSENT_AUTHZ_TABLES` shape while session callers are served. Consequence noted in ③: at this seam a false positive restores the fall-through, not only the quiet refusal.

5. **The other `none` exits are unchanged**: no header (688), no engine or an engine without `find` (689), no row (721), a row with no `user_id` (724), each pinned beside a healthy-key control. Session-only callers never reach the read (688 returns before it), pinned on REST and settings under the same fault.

6. **`resolveApiKeyPrincipal`** (622–632) now rejects where it answered `undefined`; its docblock drops "a lookup error" and says so. In-repo users are re-exports only (core `security/index.ts` 125, runtime `security/api-key.ts` 22 and `index.ts` 44). RIGHT, and the changeset names it.

7. **The label `'sys_api_key'`.** RIGHT: the constructor's `object` is documented as the object/table whose read failed, `tryFind` labels by table (433), and the service sources keep their source labels. No non-test reader branches on `.object`; it reaches only the message text and the pins.

8. **Door pins prove what the card asks, with controls.** REST: key-only, key-plus-cookie (service never called), session-only served as the cookie's user, healthy key served as its owner with and without a cookie, unprovisioned table `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. Settings: the same five, session reads counted. Core: the brand, code, status, object and `cause`; key-plus-cookie through `resolveAuthzContext` with `getSession` called zero times; both missing-table spellings; the other-relation phrase; the five `none` exits; a healthy control. Runtime: the flipped pin plus the moved control. Fixtures refuse combinators and unknown operator shapes rather than matching them. Gap, not a defect: no committed door pin for key-plus-cookie on the runtime dispatcher or on the storage family; the seam-level pin covers the composition both use, and the dev's M1 reading covered the runtime. Ablation as reported on the PR (8 red: 3+2+2+1, controls green) was read, not re-run.
